comment: The tool-aware library. Two tool types over the shared tag vocabulary apex/a/b/c: habst_tool, an ethynyl on a handle with a charged/spent state pair, and probe, a bare tip with no symbolic state and an empty tool side. The legs of both frames come off the handle, not off the business axis, so the four entries are not coplanar - which is what makes a mirrored molecule fail the residual instead of binding mirrored. Operations cover all three methods.

tools.name: habst_tool
tools.note: Hydrogen abstraction tool: an ethynyl radical on a handle. The apex carbon is at the origin, the second carbon 1.21 A below it and the handle carbon at 2.66 A; the three legs are the cage atoms around the handle carbon, 3.17 A below the apex.

tools.name: probe
tools.note: A bare probe, for lithography: it visits a site and changes nothing about itself. No states, and an empty tool side.

ops.name: habst
ops.note: Hydrogen abstraction by the charged tool: the H leaves the workpiece and arrives at the tool's apex.

ops.name: habst_probe
ops.note: The same abstraction performed by a bare probe - a different reaction by the environment-variant convention, sharing only the target-side pattern. Its tool side is empty, so the step records which instrument visited without asserting any change.

ops.name: hdump
ops.note: The recharge: the spent tool dumps its hydrogen onto a bare atom of a reservoir and comes back charged.

ops.name: settle
ops.note: A rearrangement the workpiece performs by itself: one atom moves 0.2 A.

ops.name: bridge
ops.note: Bonds two atoms 2.5 A apart. The only operation here whose before pattern names two atoms, which is what makes a match spanning two participants possible at all.

ops.name: expose
ops.note: One site's share of an X2 exposure: an X lands on a bare atom.

ops.name: expose_uv
ops.note: A second bulk agent, so a test can see one event end and another begin.

ops.name: habst_approach
ops.note: Carries the milestone-2 approach pose, which milestone 1 parses and keeps and reads for nothing.
